prompt: In a two-column proof about a bridge truss, two triangles share the side $\overline{BD}$, and a step reads "$\overline{BD} \cong \overline{BD}$." Which property of congruence is the reason for that step? Answer with one word.
hint: The step says a segment is congruent to ITSELF.

hints.text: The step says a segment is congruent to ITSELF.
The three properties are reflexive (itself), symmetric (flip sides), and transitive (chain through a middle).
A figure congruent to itself is the Reflexive Property.

explanation: The Reflexive Property says any segment or angle is congruent to itself: $\overline{BD} \cong \overline{BD}$.
It looks obvious, but in a two-column proof every statement needs a written reason — and this is the reason for a shared side.
This step is how a shared side earns its place as one of the three parts in an SSS or SAS argument.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three properties, three pictures
steps: Reflexive: a mirror — the figure and itself.
Symmetric: a flip — if $A \cong B$ then $B \cong A$. Transitive: a chain — if $A \cong B$ and $B \cong C$ then $A \cong C$. A shared side is the mirror case.
